subject.title: Skipped group messages behind requireMention do not reach message hooks, which blocks full-history archive plugins

question: Should OpenClaw expose mention-skipped/pre-session inbound content to trusted installed plugins through a public read-only hook, and must that hook be gated before release?
rationale: Current main intentionally keeps skipped-message visibility internal and opt-in; making it a public Plugin SDK hook changes what third-party plugins can observe before session dispatch and mention gating.

options.title: Gate the public hook before landing
options.body: Add an explicit operator/plugin permission or access gate, document the privacy boundary, and land the narrow hook only after that contract is visible.

options.title: Approve installed-plugin trust
options.body: Maintainers can accept that any installed plugin registering the hook may observe skipped inbound content without an extra gate.

options.title: Keep internal ingest only
options.body: Reject or pause the public hook and leave full-fidelity archive plugins dependent on internal hooks or channel-specific integrations.

recommendation.title: Gate the public hook before landing
recommendation.body: Add an explicit operator/plugin permission or access gate, document the privacy boundary, and land the narrow hook only after that contract is visible.

likelyOwner.reason: This account authored the current internal skipped-message ingest path and is the clearest history owner for deciding whether that boundary should become public.
